Dumping everything in a dish are my favourite dinners for those low energy days. All I had to do pretty much was boil some pasta! 🙌🏼 
Recipe serves 2-3 people:
✨Place 2 pieces of Salmon, 1 block of feta, 200g cherry or plum tomatoes, 2 handfuls of spinach, 1 tablespoon pesto, seasoning of choice, drizzle of olive oil into a dish.
✨Cook for 30 minutes on 170c (fan assisted oven)
✨Add 200g cooked pasta and a tablespoon of pasta water and mix
✨Serve with grated cheese of choice! 
.

What’s one job you’ve been putting off because your brain keeps telling you it’ll take ages? 👀

After so many of you asked me to do another one, here’s round two of timing the jobs I’ve been avoiding to see how long they actually take ⏱️

I’ve realised my brain is really good at convincing me that certain jobs are going to take forever… so I keep putting them off but this little experiment is definitely helping to retrain my brain!

This week’s results:
✨ Windows: procrastinated for 5 weeks - actually took 12 minutes 53 seconds

✨ Chairs: procrastinated for 3 weeks - actually took 11 minutes and 21 seconds 

This week I also realised something else… I kept waiting until I felt motivated to start, but the motivation came once I’d got going! 

Now tell me… what’s been sitting on your to-do list for weeks (or even months)? 👇

items.caption:
My DMs have been busy with requests about this, so here’s 4 DIY fly repellent hacks I’ve found online that are definitely worth trying 🪰✨

1. Fill a saucepan halfway with water, add 1 sliced lemon, 1–2 sprigs of rosemary, 10–20 cloves and 10–20 drops of lemongrass essential oil. Bring to the boil, then simmer. Top up the water as and when needed — refresh every couple of days when the scent starts to fade.
2. Sprinkle cinnamon around the base and inside the lid of your bins to help deter flies from hanging around those unwanted smells 🗑️
3. Add cloves to half a lemon and place it in your fruit bowl to help keep fruit flies away 🍋
4. Place mint near an open window to help discourage flies from coming in 🌿

Which one will you try first? 👇
.
#cleaninghacks #lifehacks #homehacks #cleaningtips #cleaningaccount

items.transcript: Here's four DIY fly repellent hacks that I learned from the internet that you might want to try too. To keep them out the kitchen, use a simmer pot of lemon, rosemary, cloves and lemongrass essential oil. They also hate the smell of cinnamon so adding some to your bin outside is a really easy way to keep them away from that. Adding cloves to half a lemon and popping it in your fruit bowl will mean that you won't have any fruit flies. And finally, having a herb like mint next to an open window will stop them from coming in.

items.caption:
The only background noise my brain is accepting from now on 😂

This is one of those jobs I’ve been meaning to do for ages and I’m so glad I finally did.🌿💦 

I’ve wanted a little water feature for a while, but didn’t want to spend a fortune so decided to DIY it. All you need is two planters, bricks (although I thought afterwards I could’ve just filled the whole planter with soil 🤔), a few flowers, white decorative stones and a solar fountain. 

I love how it finishes off this corner of the garden. The sound of the water just adds that little bit of zen. And adding wheels to the base means that I can move it around when I get bored and want a change ✨

#diygarden #diyhomeprojects #diywaterfountain #diyhomedecor #gardendecor

items.transcript: I've wanted to add a bit of zen to the garden and make one of these DIY water fountains for a while now. Not sure why I chose to do it during a heatwave because I was sweating, but wait to see how it turns out because it was so worth it. You don't have to add wheels to the base, but I just did it so I could move it around the garden whenever I fancied a change. And this is the clever bit, it's a solar-powered fountain, so there's nothing complicated to it and I don't know why I've been putting it off for so long because it is so easy.

Try this 10-minute Big Mac taco for those low-energy days 🌮🍔

100g mince pressed onto a regular wrap, seasoned with salt & pepper, then cooked mince-side down for around 5 minutes. Flip, add a square of cheese and cook for a further 3 minutes until melted.

Finish with salad, gherkins and burger sauce for the ultimate Big Mac-inspired fakeaway 😍

Quick, easy and perfect for those days when you want something tasty without the effort.
